alt_text: Detect blinks faster with linear transformers. The page features a large illustration of an eye, introducing the topic of fast blink detection using linear transformers.

The Blink Detection Challenge discusses that detecting eye blinks is challenging because it reveals deep fakes and driver drowsiness. Existing methods struggle with short blinks due to frame-wise classification.
Introducing BlinkLinMulT, a fast transformer-based framework for eye blink detection that combines low- and high-level feature sequences including head pose angles.
BlinkLinMulT is a multimodal transformer architecture for blink presence detection and frame-wise eye state recognition.
The page shows superior cross-dataset results, stating that BlinkLinMulT matches or beats state-of-the-art methods and achieves a perfect 1.0 F1 score on the TalkingFace dataset.
Robustness via Union Training. Union training improved F1 scores on CEW, ZJU, and RT-BENEimg benchmarks. Eye state recognition and blink detection outperformed single dataset baselines.
Model performance drops at higher yaw angles. The chart shows head pose angle dependence of BlinkLinMulT for blink presence detection.
The BlinkLinMulT model is trained once on the union of all datasets, improving robustness and results across all individual unseen datasets.
